note: The public version ladder. `version` and `phase` must equal the private roadmap's ladder, row for row (the ladder gate, `cargo xtask ci`); `summary` is written for the site and never copied from a private document. States: done, planned, goal, later.

rungs.summary: The foundation: its own bootloader checks a signed system image and paints the screen, and every quality check runs on every change.
Freally Core, the kernel: memory, interrupts, timers, a scheduler and messages. The first program starts, and a crash leaves a report.
Services and drivers: every processor core, the screen, keyboard and mouse, and updates that fall back on their own if they fail.
First light: the desktop, a terminal, a shell, and Monitor, which explains every process. The desktop in under 3 seconds.
The real laptop: Freally OS starts from a USB stick on its first laptop.
Developer tools: replace a running service in place, and roll it back, without a restart.
Storage, encrypted local accounts, Settings and Files.
The tester build: signed releases, offline updates and a private image for testers.
Networking, and online updates that ask first.
USB.
Sound.
Together: invite anyone, on any computer or phone, by a link or a QR code, to work with you in the apps you share.
Freally's own programming language, first version.
The app sandbox, and Freally Guard.
Linux programs in the terminal.
Freally OS builds itself.
Trackpad, battery, brightness and sleep.
Wi-Fi.
Pictures, your own background, and Photos.
The first wave of apps.
The browser: the web without scripts.
The browser: JavaScript.
Browser extensions and web protection.
Graphics acceleration.
Documents.
Spreadsheets.
Presentations.
Media: a player, a recorder and the camera.
Mail and contacts.
Windows programs: console programs.
Windows programs: windowed apps.
Mac programs: command-line tools.
Mac programs: windowed apps.
Mac programs: apps made only for Apple silicon.
The Freally music apps, with VST3 and CLAP plugins.
Every setting, every language, and a screen reader.
Install to the computer's own drive.
The beta: every feature frozen, tested and written down.
The release candidate: every feature tested on real hardware.
Version 1.0, and the first download.
After 1.0: one version at a time.
